localBiteReport: The most current report available (week of September 4–10, 2026) comes from Capt. Blake Nelson with Last Cast Charters, who covers Choctawhatchee Bay weekly for the Northwest Florida Fishing Report. Water temp is 87°F. The bay is showing early signs of the fall transition: large schools of baitfish (greenies/pogies) are moving from deeper open water onto flats, into bayous, and around bridge areas — a signal that redfish and trout activity on the flats should improve as September pushes toward October. Slot redfish on the flats are expected to pick up significantly with the upcoming fall mullet run, with the second or third week of September historically being the first meaningful opportunity; bull reds are also being reported patrolling deeper channels and around the East Pass jetties. Speckled trout are holding around grass, sandy pockets, docks, and deeper cuts, and are responding to soft plastics and live bait. Overall, the bay bite is in a transitional lull between summer and fall patterns — conditions are building toward what guides expect to be one of the better inshore stretches of the year.
